English

Generated Narrative: CodeSystem KGRecommendationKind

This case-sensitive code system http://smart.who.int/base/CodeSystem/KGRecommendationKind defines the following codes:

CodeDisplayDefinition
recommendation RecommendationA graded recommendation, with a direction and a strength. Handbook §10.4.
context-specific Context specificRecommended only in specified contexts or settings, stated in the recommendation. ANC guideline (2016) Table 1, verified.
research-context Research contextRecommended only in the context of rigorous research. ANC guideline (2016) Table 1, verified.
good-practice-statement Good practice statementAn ungraded statement whose benefit is so clear that grading the evidence is not a useful exercise. Carries no strength or certainty. Guyatt et al. 2016.
no-recommendation No recommendation"No recommendation can be made because…" — the guideline development group decided the evidence could not support one. Handbook §10.7. Distinct from very-low certainty: absent evidence and weak evidence are different findings.

name: KGRecommendationKind
title: Knowledge graph L1: recommendation kind
description: What sort of normative statement this is. Grading is optional: ANC 2016 prints a direction ('Recommended', 'Not recommended') and no GRADE strength. A strength always needs a direction. A good practice statement and a no-recommendation carry no strength or certainty, and a no-recommendation carries no direction. Source: smart-kg ontology/l1/l1.json valueSets "recommendation-kind"; WHO handbook §10.4, §10.7; ANC guideline (2016) Table 1, verified; Guyatt et al. 2016 on good practice statements.
